metadata.case_name: KU CHIU CHUNG WOODY v. TANG TIN SUNG

plaintiff.occupation_before: Senior B Cook at La Cite Restaurant (Pacific Place)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Junior clerk with Plenty More Credit Management Salary Limited

injuries.description: close fracture of the left acetabulum with dislocation of the left hip

source: open fracture of the left proximal tibia
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of tibia, unspecified

source: open complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament of the left knee

source: open partial tear of the lateral meniscus of the left knee

injuries.description: closed fracture of the shaft of the left tibia
source: closed fracture of the shaft of the left tibia

manifestations.description: He walks unaided at home and within short distances from home if he walks slowly. He cannot walk unaided for long direction, because the left hip feels weak, and the left knee is painful. When he walks for longer distances, he would rely on a cane.
His left lower limb feels weak if he stands unaided for half an hour. He has to rely more on the right side for continual standing.
He is not able to squat.
His left knee and ankle are stiff.
He feels weakness in the left lower limb in walking up for 1-2 flights of stairs.
There is occasional tight feeling along the posterior left thigh and calf.

treatments_received: open reduction of the left hip and internal fixation of the left acetabular fracture
open reduction and internal fixation of the left proximal tibia
closed reduction of the tibia shaft fracture with external fixator
repeated operation for adjustment of the tibial shaft fracture performed on 18th November, 1998
readmission for readjustment of the external fixator on 12th January, 1999
out-patient follow-up and physiotherapy treatments (Caritas Medical Centre 14 times; Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital 51 times; Chai Wan Health Centre 33 times)
external fixator removed in about mid 1999
progressed to walking with a cane
treatments_future: further physiotherapy course of 30 to 40 treatments (suggested by Dr. Chiang)

losses.description: Walks unaided only at short distances, requires a cane for longer distances, cannot squat, left knee and ankle stiffness, weakness on standing and climbing stairs
Unable to maintain his pre-accident occupation as a cook requiring prolonged standing; choice of employment more restricted
